ctx.x: Little Brother recorded a song and it was I think in 1952. It had something to do with the Victory Club.

This was one Sunday morning boy. And old Papa Ammons was over there, Abbot, before he passed. Boy you talking about some fun we had. He and Papa Yassid, they double headed the piano boy. And we danced there that morning till 9, 10 o'clock. That reminds me of Bigfoot Clows at the Victory Club. You ever heard Bigfoot Clows play? He and Sweet Frank Williams. Along about 3 or 4 o'clock in the morning, Milt Moore and Jack Teagarden came by. I run into a little girl with a green dress on and some red stocket. Boy that…

A classic by Little Brother Montgomery, to say the least. And I'd like to remind you, this is WLDC at Loyola University, and we're in New Orleans. And we're doing an interview with Mrs. Lee Collins, whose husband is Trumpeter Lee Collins. And she has written a book, and it's entitled, Oh, Didn't He Ramble? And we're trying to talk about Lee and something about the book and get into a few things about it. What inspired you to write a book about your husband? Well, Lee.
